owner_direction: Use TradingView Desktop as the visual and interaction benchmark for ScopeHub. The owner offered the locally installed application and morluto/rea as possible aids and delegated the method to development.

reference_sources.name: REA
reference_sources.assessment: REA supports investigation of application behavior and internals. A normal UI session, screenshots and input replay are sufficient for this comparison. Tool choice remains open.

installed_desktop.session: Fresh signed-out profile in a 1152 by 864 window on an isolated 1440 by 900 display at 1x.
installed_desktop.observed: A centered welcome dialog offered sign-in through a browser. Closing it exited this session. The desktop chart, tab handling and return focus were unobserved.

public_chart.observed: The chart occupied most of the window between the left tool rail and right watchlist. The symbol control in the top toolbar opened a centered search field and results over the still-visible chart. The current symbol text was selected in the focused input. Escape closed the search and kept the same chart symbol.

scopehub.surface: Ubuntu browser development preview with synthetic instruments
scopehub.case: open the chart workspace, find symbols from the keyboard and inspect bars in the side panel
scopehub.observed: The chart occupied most of the window with the symbol control above it, tools on the left and the watchlist on the right. Search focused the input. Escape dismissed it and restored focus to its opener. Arrow keys changed the highlighted result and Enter selected it.

matched_dark_layout.conditions: Browser client area of 1366 by 900 logical pixels at 1x on both surfaces. Dark theme selected in the public Supercharts menu and active in the synthetic ScopeHub preview.
matched_dark_layout.measurement: Read horizontal chart-panel edges between the left tool rail and the right watchlist, including the price scale and excluding the dividers. Read the first content row below the top toolbar.
matched_dark_layout.finding: Both layouts give the chart about seven tenths of the window width. ScopeHub reserves ten more vertical pixels above the chart. Review this difference alongside legibility and usable chart space in the native desktop.

follow_up: M1-012 compares the integrated ScopeHub desktop journeys. Use matching themes and scale when judging color or density. Record the reference host and focus or selection after dismissal. The observations here cover a signed-out native entry and two browser surfaces.
